title: AMF: SMF discovery failure in PDU session establishment may accumulate AMF PDU session contexts  #1
body:
### Summary

The AMF registers a `pdu_session_context` into the UE context. 
When SMF selection then fails, `amf_sbi::handle_itti_message(itti_nsmf_pdusession_create_sm_context&)` returns without calling the release API, `ue_context::remove_pdu_sessions_context()`. The context stays live in `ue_context::pdu_sessions` for a PDU session.

Cleanup exists but all of it is driven by the SMF. A context the SMF never learned about is reachable by none of it. The PoC confirms one surviving context per PDU session identity, zero releases, and one `wait_for_result()` timeout charged to `TASK_AMF_N1` per survivor at de-registration.

### Details

Source analysis on `v2.2.1` (April 2026), AMF commit `513c0f2`.

**1. The context is registered before SMF selection** 

https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-amf/blob/513c0f2dc4175e7d8f099a41d4a797913d3cf40e/src/amf-app/amf_sbi.cpp#L425-L432


`ue_context::add_pdu_session_context()`  inserts into `pdu_sessions`, keyed by PDU session identity. From here every consumer that enumerates the UE's sessions sees it.

**2. The failure point** 

https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-amf/blob/513c0f2dc4175e7d8f099a41d4a797913d3cf40e/src/amf-app/amf_sbi.cpp#L497-L502


**3. The release API is never reached.**

https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-amf/blob/513c0f2dc4175e7d8f099a41d4a797913d3cf40e/src/contexts/ue_context.cpp#L67-L75

`ue_context::remove_pdu_sessions_context()` has exactly three call sites, all requiring an SMF that knows the session:

- `amf_app.cpp:482` — driven by `SMContextStatusNotify` from the SMF
- `amf_n1.cpp:4394` — de-registration, inside the `http_response_code == OK || NO_CONTENT` branch
- `amf_app.cpp:2851` — PDU session release handling

**4. De-registration enumerates the survivors but cannot clean them.**

https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-amf/blob/513c0f2dc4175e7d8f099a41d4a797913d3cf40e/src/amf-app/amf_n1.cpp#L4334-L4366

https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-amf/blob/513c0f2dc4175e7d8f099a41d4a797913d3cf40e/src/common/amf_sbi_helper.cpp#L105-L108

`amf_n1.cpp:4334-4366` dispatches one release ITTI per session; the SBI handler rejects each at `amf_sbi.cpp:685-689` via `amf_sbi_helper.cpp:105-108` (`No SMF is available for this PDU session`), so the HTTP-status-gated removal at `amf_n1.cpp:4394` never runs. The promise is also never set, so the serial waiter at `amf_n1.cpp:4375` runs to timeout — `KFutureStatusTimeoutMs = 1000` (`oai-cn5g-common-src`, `utils/utils.hpp:18,32-46`), on the single `TASK_AMF_N1` thread.

### PoC

The SMF was left down, so SMF selection fails. One UE then attempts several PDU sessions and deregisters. No source change.
```
contexts registered  ("Created a PDU Session Context") : 3
failure returns taken ("SMF Selection, no SMF candidate is available") : 7
contexts released  ("PDU Session ID N removed") : 0
still in the map at de-registration  ("No SMF is available for this PDU session") : 3
```

Counts of AMF log lines over one run, from a freshly started AMF.

- Nothing is released. 7 failure returns, 0 release log lines.
- They were all still there. De-registration walks pdu_sessions and sends a release for each entry, so the last count is a direct readout of the map: 3 registered, 3 still present.
- Accumulation is per PDU session identity, not per attempt. 7 failures produced 3 contexts because get_pdu_session_context() at :427 finds and reuses the survivor on retry, so T3580 retransmissions do not allocate again.

The stall appears after dispatch, in the serial wait loop:

```text
22:18:50.679013179 [amf_sbi][error] No SMF is available for this PDU session
22:18:50.679061054 [amf_sbi][error] No SMF is available for this PDU session
22:18:50.679064512 [amf_sbi][error] No SMF is available for this PDU session
22:18:53.685150138 [nas_mm][debug]  Size of Deregistration Accept message 3
```

3.006 s against 3 survivors and a 1000 ms timeout. The contexts were freed only when the ue_context itself was destroyed — a consequence of the UE going away, not a rollback of the failed transaction.

### Impact

The trigger needs no unusual configuration: an SMF that is down, restarting, or not yet registered with the NRF, or a lost AMF-to-NRF path, all end at the same `discover_smf()` failure. While that lasts, every PDU session attempt leaves a context behind.

Those contexts are not inert. Several places walk the UE's session list — de-registration at `amf_n1.cpp:4334` and `:5891`, Service Request and Initial Context Setup at `amf_n2.cpp:1612` and `:2233` — and each of them treats a survivor as a real PDU session, while the UE believes it has none. `ue_context::copy_pdu_sessions()` (`ue_context.cpp:52-54`, called from `amf_n1.cpp:930`, `:1377` and `:2157`) also copies them into the new `ue_context` on re-registration, so they outlive a single attach; this is from the code, not measured here.

The memory itself is bounded: `pdu_sessions` is keyed by PDU session identity, so retries overwrite rather than accumulate, and everything is freed with the `ue_context`.

The cost that shows up in practice is delay. `TASK_AMF_N1` is a single thread and handles NAS for every UE. When a UE deregisters, the AMF walks its session list and waits on each release in turn; a survivor has no SMF to send to, so that wait runs the full `KFutureStatusTimeoutMs` before giving up. Three survivors cost three seconds, and during those seconds no other UE's NAS is processed. After an SMF outage, every affected UE carries its own survivors into the same queue.
